content:
Apple's annual September event will be held this Wednesday, when the company will unveil three brand-new iPhone models: the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and iPhone Ultra. Here's a preview roundup for everyone.

iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max

The iPhone 18 Pro and iPhone 18 Pro Max will succeed the widely popular 17 Pro series, becoming the new generation of flagship models.

According to circulating rumours, the new features include:

  • Equipped with the A20 Pro chip, with performance and power efficiency taken to the next level
  • Major upgrades to the camera system, with the main lens adding a variable aperture design
  • Dynamic Island reduced by 35%, giving a sleeker and more modern look
  • New colour options debut, headlined by a bold wine-red shade
  • The best battery life ever, with particularly significant gains on the iPhone 18 Pro Max
  • Camera Control button redesigned for a completely refreshed user experience
  • Adoption of Apple's in-house C2 cellular modem
  • Addition of new satellite features, including 5G satellite connectivity

The starting price of the iPhone 18 Pro is expected to rise. Market estimates put it from US$1,399 onwards, though the author believes the actual pricing may be closer to US$1,199 or US$1,249.

iPhone Ultra

The iPhone Ultra is reportedly going to be the name of Apple's first foldable device, with expected pricing above US$2,000, carving out an entirely new premium market positioning.

The folding design will make the iPhone Ultra the most breakthrough model Apple has ever launched. The body adopts a wide book-style fold, with the outer display at roughly 5.4 inches and the inner display at 7.8 inches, delivering an experience close to the iPad mini.

The body materials are expected to follow the iPhone Air, using a titanium frame for a clean, minimalist look.

The iPhone Ultra will feature two rear lenses (main and ultra-wide), plus two front-facing lenses corresponding to the inner and outer displays. It will use Touch ID rather than Face ID for unlocking.

Software will be the biggest highlight of this device, working with iOS 27 to support side-by-side multitasking and adaptive landscape layout, fully unleashing the advantages of the new foldable form factor.

Performance is expected to be on par with the iPhone 18 Pro, also featuring the A20 Pro chip, adding a vapour chamber cooling design, and equipped with the C2 modem.

The missing members: iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2

As usual, beyond the flagships, Apple also launches a brand-new base iPhone 18 and an iPhone Air successor each September.

However, reports say Apple will significantly adjust its autumn product line this year, pushing the iPhone 18 and iPhone Air 2 back to early 2027.

It remains unclear whether this arrangement is purely a strategic consideration or whether it's forced by the current memory shortage. Either way, the absence of more affordable models means this autumn's new iPhone lineup will be entirely focused on the high-end market.

Will readers be upgrading to a new iPhone this autumn? Which model is your pick? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments section.
